summary:
MasterX-Space-Game is an interactive space mission design and simulation platform that allows users to design, configure, and evaluate a complete spacecraft mission. Starting with a CubeSat Earth-observation mission, users select spacecraft components and make engineering decisions involving mass, power, budget, communication, storage, and subsystem compatibility.

The platform connects engineering calculations with a mission simulation engine to demonstrate how design decisions influence spacecraft performance, mission operations, resource constraints, and mission outcomes.

MasterX aims to make space mission engineering more accessible and engaging through interactive experimentation and visual storytelling.
details:
MasterX-Space-Game provides an interactive environment for spacecraft mission design and simulation.

Users configure a spacecraft by selecting components from an engineering catalogue. The engineering engine evaluates the spacecraft configuration, calculating mass, power generation and consumption, battery capacity, budget, data generation, storage, communication capability, and compatibility constraints.

The simulation engine models mission operations, including orbital behaviour, power-system performance, imaging, data storage, ground communication, mission stages, and anomalies. Users can observe the consequences of engineering decisions and understand why a mission succeeds or encounters failures.

Technology stack:

  • React and TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Three.js and React Three Fiber
  • React Router
  • Lucide icons

The project combines engineering calculations, simulation logic, and interactive visual communication to explain the complexity of space mission planning.
dataRefs: NASA CubeSat 101: Basic Concepts and Processes for First-Time CubeSat Developers
